about: R2 (P-230 (7)): the dated fee table, data and never code. Each line cites IRCC's page, quote and date (P-170). Status: Researched (source, date): may change; Sample until the immigration expert confirms (P-171). Sources: the IRCC fee list itself for the study permit, work permit, open work permit holder and visitor extension lines (read 2026-11-03); research_notes/visitor-visa-and-six-combinations-research-2026-11-02.md rows 1a, 1b, 1c; product/screens/W1-baseline/immigration-facts-2026-10-29.md row 19. Each line carries its basis (P-247): per_application (once per application filed), per_person_by_role (each person of the named roles), per_position (not worked out yet), or family_maximum (each person, capped once enough people apply together). M3-S1 (P-425, read 2026-11-10): a per_application line may name a role that co-files (the sponsor: takes part, never applies), and is then charged on that person's co-filed application, which carries its own fees; a combination's settings (each_files_own, co_filed_why) are data here, never code. A fee change is an edit to this file with its test (tests/check_r2_fee_table.ts, run by CI). Part 2 of R2 moves it into a stored library table frozen with each release (setup S7a, PUT /library/fees). BK-8 (P-448): a line's step names the IRCC step it pays for (biometrics); the prepare view finds a combination's biometrics step and its ages by it, so a pathway lists its own line (one per step), never another pathway's.

sp.outside.basis_note: Each family member files their own application and pays for the document they apply for: the student a study permit; a child who will study 6 months or more a study permit (Sample); any other child a visitor visa; a spouse or partner a work permit with the open work permit holder fee. Sample until the immigration expert confirms: which spouses qualify for an open work permit (program level and length), a child from a visa-exempt country (who needs an eTA, not a visitor visa), and whether a family member going to Québec needs their own CAQ (not priced here).
sp.outside.note: BK-15 (R-e, P-486, BK-13 dry run gap C5): fees per family member as data. Each role's filing and fee lines are fees_by_role; a child who studies files the study permit their line adds instead of the visitor visa (samples/conditional-filings.json names its fee lines). Amounts are the fee table's own lines (IRCC fee list, cited on each line). C6.17 (P-444, QA-375): its per-person checklist is its release's document lines (worked out for every combination since M3-S4, P-425), each cited from IMM 5483 (08-2025) (samples/form-setup.json sp.outside documentsCited).

fs.spouse.label: Spouse or common-law partner sponsorship
fs.spouse.co_filed_why: The sponsorship and the principal's application are sent together and cannot be split (IRCC: the principal "will submit both applications together online").
fs.spouse.note: M3-S1 (P-425): two filings in one submission, the sponsor's co-filed sponsorship application and the principal's permanent residence application (canada.ca "Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Apply", saved 2026-10-27: "there are 2 applications: Sponsorship application … Permanent residence application"). The sponsorship carries its own fee (spouse_sponsorship, per application, role sponsor); the principal's application carries the right of permanent residence fee and each dependent child's fee. Modes as the release's lines (samples/wave1.json). Biometrics are not listed: the table's biometrics line carries the temporary residents' exemptions (under 14, over 79), and IRCC's permanent residence page names no upper age, so the case says in words (basis_note) that its total leaves them out; a cited permanent residence biometrics line is a follow-up. Sample until the immigration expert confirms (P-171).
fs.spouse.basis_note: Biometrics are not in this total: IRCC asks permanent residence applicants for them ("You must give your biometrics every time you apply for permanent residence", canada.ca When to give your biometrics – permanent resident applicants, 2026-03-30; fee list: CAD 85 a person, CAD 170 for a family of 2 or more), but their exemptions for permanent residence are not in the fee table yet, so nothing is guessed.
